subject: SummitCare evaluation readout & safety action plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@summitcare.health>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@summitcare.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + safety/readout artifacts (SummitCare)

Hi Alex, Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today. Per our call, I wanted to consolidate the evaluation readout, model recommendations, and a short safety action plan so we can align on next steps. High level: SummitCare is a strong fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) given PHI considerations; primary goals are throughput for triage routing and strict refusal behavior for treatment recommendations.

Key findings from the quick eval we ran (attached CSV):
- Recommended model family: redwood-inference-6b-int8 for baseline latency/cost tradeoff; redwood-inference-14b-qat for higher accuracy on clinical summarization.
- Benchmark highlights: 95th perc latency < 180ms on 512-token average payload for 6b-int8 with continuous batching; 14b-qat shows +6% accuracy on our clinical NER/QA prompts but 2x token cost.
- Prompt sets: attached prompt_set_v1.txt contains the scoring prompts we used for safety/refusal checks and a set of guardrail templates (disallowed_actions / triage_only / escalate_to_human).

Safety/regulatory concerns surfaced:
- Refusal coverage: current baseline rejects direct treatment instructions ~82% of time on adversarial rephrasings. We recommend adding explicit refusal templates and a gated escalation path for borderline queries.
- Sensitive domain policy: mental health and medication dosing require deterministic escalation and an explicit human-in-loop flag in outputs.
- Auditability: include token-level logging with redaction filters for PHI; we've noted this in the private deployment checklist.

Next steps (proposed, owners, ETA):
1) Share full benchmark CSV and prompt set (attachments) — Sergio (done)
2) Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence request — Alex: share timeline; Redwood to assign Neha for responses (ETA 3 business days)
3) Run a 48-hour focused safety eval with adversarial prompts on 14b-qat and 6b-int8 — Soojin to run (ETA 72 hours)
4) Draft SOW for pilot (10k monthly tokens/day throughput) and the dedicated pool sizing — Ben to draft SOW (ETA 2 business days)

Attachments: summitcare_eval_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, redwood_sow_draft.pdf (placeholder).

If this looks right I’ll schedule a short follow-up next Wednesday with Neha and Soojin to review the safety eval plan.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@summitcare.health>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + safety/readout artifacts (SummitCare)

Thanks Sergio — very clear and helpful summary. A few notes from our side: we absolutely need the deterministic escalation on medication dosing (no exceptions) and a log export we can ingest into our SIEM. Priya and I will validate the benchmark numbers with our infra team; the latency figures look promising.

Action items on our end:
- Priya will assemble the procurement timeline and internal security contact list by EOD Thursday.
- I'll share an initial list of high-risk prompt patterns we've observed in production (mostly rephrasings that try to coerce treatment specifics).

Confirming we want the 48-hour safety eval — please run the adversarial suite and include the refusal templates you mentioned.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Director of Product, SummitCare Health
alex.rivera@summitcare.health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@summitcare.health>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@summitcare.health>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + safety/readout artifacts (SummitCare)

Alex/Priya — quick note from the product/ops side. Two clarifications before we run the expanded safety suite: 

1) Can you confirm expected peak concurrent sessions and typical avg tokens per session? (we need this to size the dedicated pool accurately for the pilot).
2) On escalation semantics: we will implement a structured output with an H|E flag (HumanEscalate boolean) in the model response and a short refusal rationale field. That helps your SIEM correlation and audit.

Sooj and I will collaborate on hardening the guardrail templates. Sooj — for the adversarial run please add these variants to prompt_set_v1: explicit dosing rephrases, roleplay as clinician, and chain-of-thought attempts to bypass refusal. Capture pass/fail and the failure mode (silent omission, incorrect answer, or partial disclosure).

We should also align contractually on data retention/redaction in the SOW. Ben — can you include the retention and logging SLAs in the SOW draft?

Thanks — Marissa
Head of Product | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@summitcare.health>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@summitcare.health>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + safety/readout artifacts (SummitCare) — security Qs + next steps

Hi Alex/Priya — looping in answers to immediate security/compliance asks and next steps for evidence: 

1) SOC2 + pen test: we can provide our SOC2 Type II report and recent pen test summary. I will send the secure share link to the procurement contact once we have the NDA/procurement contact.
2) SIEM export: we support S3-compatible event export with token redaction and a second metrics-only stream (no PHI) for analytics. We will include field-level redaction for patient identifiers in the SOW.
3) Adversarial safety eval: Soojin will run the 48-hour suite in isolated infra with the following outputs: pass/fail matrix, failure examples (redacted), and recommended guardrail templates. I'll review and add compliance notes before we hand to SummitCare.

Deliverables and ETA:
- Security evidence package (SOC2 + pen test) — Neha (ETA 2 business days after NDA)
- Safety eval report (redacted) + updated prompt_set_v1 (with adversarial variants) — Soojin/Neha (ETA 3 business days)
- Draft SOW including retention, logging SLAs, and escalation flow — Ben (ETA 2 business days)

If you can share the procurement contact and any internal compliance checklist, we’ll accelerate the evidence handoff.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.inference
